overview: This Senate resolution names July 15, 2026, as "Glioblastoma Awareness Day." Glioblastoma is the most common and most aggressive cancerous brain tumor; the resolution notes its very low five-year survival rate, the lack of screening tests, and that few treatments have been approved for it. It honors people who have died from or are living with the disease and supports their families and caregivers. It encourages more public awareness, better treatments, molecular biomarker testing (lab tests of the tumor's genetic makeup used in diagnosis), and continued research, including through a National Cancer Institute network that develops new therapies. It does not create programs or spend money. As of June 23, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say drawing attention to one of the deadliest cancers can encourage research, earlier testing and support for patients and families.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding for glioblastoma research or treatment.
